title: Scholar's mate and how to stop it
line: Queen and bishop on f7 in four moves, and the moves that make it harmless.

steps.text: At the start, f7 is Black's weakest square: only the king guards it. Put your bishop where it aims at f7.
steps.hint: The bishop needs one move to reach a square that aims at f7.
steps.after: The bishop looks straight at f7.

steps.text: Bring your queen to h5. Now the queen and the bishop both aim at f7.
steps.after: Two pieces aim at f7, and only the king defends it.

steps.text: Black attacks your queen with the knight and forgets about f7. Finish the game.

wrong.h5e5: That is check, but the knight on c6 takes your queen.
wrong.c4f7: That is check, but the king steps to e7 and there is no mate.

steps.after: Checkmate. The bishop guards the queen, and the king has no square to go to.

steps.text: That is Scholar's mate. Now take Black's side, after the queen has come to h5, and stop it.
Stop the mate on f7 with a pawn move that also attacks the queen.

steps.text: The queen has moved twice, and the knight on c6 can attack her again from d4. Black is ahead in getting pieces out.

summary: Queen and bishop aimed at the pawn beside the king mate a careless player. Guard it, block the queen, develop.
